newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Dehaene supports UK borders opt-out.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Dehaene supports UK borders opt-out.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, spurned by Britain three years ago as European Commission president, said on Thursday he supported London's desire to keep its frontier checks with the rest of Europe.
But he said that before an opt-out was granted to Britain in a new treaty to be agreed in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17, it must offer something to its partners.
"We are willing to recognise their special concerns and to seek solutions that respond to their wishes," Dehaene said in a speech. "But we are waiting for the needed reciprocity from them."
Negotiators on the new European Union treaty are seeking to incorporate the Schengen Agreement, a pact signed by 13 EU members to lift internal border controls.
Britain is seeking both an opt-out from the plan and a legally binding statement recognising its right to keep its border controls.

Most countries have accepted this in theory -- recognising Britain's and Ireland's special status as islands -- but are expected to agree it formally only after some horse trading over other treaty issues.

Dehaene was vetoed by former British prime minister John Major at an EU summit in Corfu, Greece in June 1994. Major, under pressure from Eurosceptics at home, said Dehaene was too fervent an EU integrationist.
